Question 7

Suppose we wish to find a root of the function f(x)=ex+x3−5x in the interval [1,2]. Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting from the point x0=1.5. Round your answer to three decimal places.

EXPLANATION

The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

xn+1=xn−f(xn)f′(xn)

where f′(xn) is the derivative of f(x) evaluated at xn.

In our case, we have

f′(x)=(ex+x3−5x)′=ex+3x2−5.

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

xn+1=xn−enx+xn3−5xnenx+3xn2−5=xn(enx+3xn2−5)−(enx+xn3−5xn)enx+3xn2−5=xnexn+2xn3−exnexn+3xn2−5.

Starting with x0=1.5, we have

x1=x0ex0+2x03−ex0ex0+3x02−5=(1.5)e1.5+2(1.5)3−e1.5e1.5+3(1.5)2−5=1.442762….

x2=x1ex1+2x13−ex1ex1+3x12−5=(1.442762…)e1.442762…+2(1.442762…)3−e1.442762…e1.442762…+3(1.442762…)2−5≈1.439,

rounded to three decimal places.
